title: Новый паспорт и усы  (New Passport and Mustache)

segments.t: Chef Barinov asks if their upcoming wedding was also a cover, and Elena assures him her love is real. She gives him five minutes to say goodbye to his daughter Katya and tells him to shave off his famous mustache.
Не волнуйся, я позабочусь о них.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'And what about our wedding?' Barinov inquires calmly to make the point, leaning on "kak" ("how") before closing the thought with "svadba" ("wedding").
'Was that also your cover story?' Barinov questions evenly without a pause, combining "tozhe" ("too") and "bylo" ("was") so the key meaning lands right away.
'No, I truly love you.' Elena picks an easygoing mood for Barinov, joining "deystvitelno" ("really, indeed") to "lyublyu" ("love") so every word pulls its weight.
'That is why I am helping you escape.' Elena takes an earnest tone in the conversation, anchoring the Russian line on "poetomu" ("that's why") and "pomogayu" ("to help") without extra filler.
'Take this, it is your new passport.' Elena favors a frank angle in this beat, using "vozmi" (from "vzyat", "take, pick up") alongside "novyy" ("new") to shape the meaning.

'You must leave the country urgently.' Elena chooses an honest view across the room, building the phrase around "dolzhen" ("has to, must") and "srochno" ("urgent, urgently") for a crisp, natural delivery.

'Along the line you will reach the airport.' Elena keeps a pointed note during the exchange, putting "vetke" ("branch, twig") alongside "doberyoshsya" ("will reach") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.

'People are tied up in the room over there.' Barinov presents a natural tack as the scene unfolds, placing "tam" ("there") straight beside "nomere" ("in the hotel room") with no word for "to be" needed.
Не волнуйся, я позабочусь о них.

'Do not worry, I will take care of them.' Elena projects a thoughtful course toward Barinov, anchoring the Russian line on "volnuysya" ("worry") and "pozabochus" ("to take care of") without extra filler.

'I need to say goodbye to Katya.' Barinov presents an easygoing note beside Elena, putting "nado" ("it is necessary") alongside "poproshchatsya" ("to say goodbye") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Alright, I give you a little time.' Elena holds an unhurried attitude in the scene, putting "khorosho" ("good, fine") alongside "dayu" ("give") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'And do not forget to shave off your mustache.' Elena keeps an unhurried attitude in this beat, using "zabud" (from "zabyt", "forget") alongside "sbrit" ("to shave off") to shape the meaning.
Не волнуйся, я позабочусь о них.
Freshly shaved, Chef Barinov runs into the kitchen and dining hall, where the dream becomes so absurd he finally realizes none of it is real. Until next time!
